subject: Joseph, son of Jacob (Genesis 37 to 50), not Joseph of Nazareth
note: Evidence for Joseph's Bible figure page. Every quotation is in joseph.quotes.json and passes verify-quotes.mjs. Fetched or extracted texts are in design/saints-hub/sources/people/joseph/ (gitignored): the BSB chapters quoted (bsb-joseph-chapters.txt, one verse a line; bsb-joseph-running.txt, the same passages as running text, for quotations that cross verses), Sirach 49:15 and other deuterocanonical lines from the World English Bible British Edition (web-joseph-lines.txt), Genesis 37:3 in the KJV (kjv-genesis-37.txt, from demos/sounds-like-scripture/raw/pg10.txt), the OCA life (oca-joseph-the-patriarch.txt), the Jewish Encyclopedia article Joseph (je-joseph.txt), Strong's Hebrew 6446 (strongs-6446.txt), Gregory of Tours, History of the Franks, tr. Brehaut 1916 (gregory-of-tours-history-brehaut.txt), the parish page on Joseph the All-Comely (orthodox-net-all-comely.txt), the OCA page for Holy Monday 2026 (oca-2026-04-06-holy-monday.txt), the 2004 Roman Martyrology in English from GCatholic (gc/, all 36 pages) and the Wikipedia wikitext (wiki-joseph-genesis.raw, a lead only, never cited). The Fathers are quoted from the shared NPNF and ANF texts in sources/shared/.

life.text: Rachel conceived after long barrenness, said "God has taken away my shame", and named him Joseph: "May the LORD add to me another son." Born in Paddan-aram, before Jacob left Laban.
life.note: The page's Name fact says the name sounds like the Hebrew for 'may He add', which is the pun Genesis 30:24 makes.

life.text: Rachel died giving birth to Benjamin on the way to Ephrath (Bethlehem). Jacob's twelve sons: six of Leah, two of Rachel (Joseph, Benjamin), two of Bilhah, two of Zilpah.
life.note: Joseph was the eleventh son (OCA numbers him 11).

life.text: At seventeen, a bad report about his brothers; the robe of many colors; the brothers hated him; the dream of the sheaves; the dream of the sun, moon and eleven stars; Jacob rebuked him but kept it in mind.

Sent to Shechem, found at Dothan; 'Here comes that dreamer'; Reuben's plan to rescue him; stripped of the robe; the dry pit; Judah's 'What profit'; sold for twenty shekels of silver to the Ishmaelites (the Midianite traders passing by); the goat's blood on the robe; Jacob's mourning.
life.note: Jacob sent him 'from the Valley of Hebron' (37:14): the third moment's place.

life.text: Potiphar, officer of Pharaoh and captain of the guard, bought him; the LORD was with Joseph; put over the whole house; 'well-built and handsome'; the wife's daily asking; 'How could I do such a great evil and sin against God?'; the cloak left in her hand; her charge ('to make sport of us'); prison.
life.note: The page says 'mock' for 'make sport of', not in quotation marks.

life.text: In prison the warden put all the prisoners in his care; the cupbearer and the baker; 'Don't interpretations belong to God?'; three branches, three baskets, three days; Pharaoh's birthday; 'remember me'; the cupbearer forgot him.

After two full years, Pharaoh's two dreams; the cupbearer remembered; shaved and changed; 'I myself cannot do it'; seven years of plenty and seven of famine; a fifth of the harvest stored; 'Can we find anyone like this man, in whom the Spirit of God abides?'; signet ring, fine linen, gold chain, second chariot, 'Bow the knee!'; the name Zaphenath-paneah; Asenath daughter of Potiphera, priest of On; thirty years old; grain 'like the sand of the sea', stored in the cities; Manasseh and Ephraim named.

Ten brothers came for grain, Benjamin kept at home; they bowed with their faces to the ground; he remembered his dreams; 'You are spies!'; three days in custody; 'Surely we are being punished because of our brother'; he understood them (an interpreter stood between them) and wept; Simeon bound; silver returned in the sacks.

The second journey with Benjamin; Joseph wept in a private room; seated by age; Benjamin's portion five times larger; the silver cup in Benjamin's sack; Judah's plea and offer to stay as a slave in the boy's place.

He sent everyone out, wept so loudly the Egyptians heard; 'I am Joseph! Is my father still alive?'; 'it was not you who sent me here, but God'; the famine had lasted two years with five to come; Benjamin given three hundred shekels and five sets of clothes; 'Do not quarrel on the way!'.
life.note: Two years of famine (45:6) is the basis of the 22-year tile: sold at 17 (37:2), 30 before Pharaoh (41:46), 7 good years, 2 of famine = 39.

life.text: Jacob revived at the sight of the wagons; God at Beersheba: 'Do not be afraid to go down to Egypt'; seventy in all; Joseph met him in Goshen and wept; 'Finally I can die'.

The famine years: money, then livestock, then land and the people themselves for seed; all the land Pharaoh's except the priests'; 'reduced the people to servitude'; a fifth to Pharaoh; 'You have saved our lives'.
life.note: Told plainly, the servitude line quoted, so the page neither hides nor judges it. Ambrose's praise of the grain policy is a tidbit, in his own words.

life.text: Jacob lived seventeen years in Egypt; the crossed hands over Ephraim and Manasseh; 'Not so, my father!'; 'I know, my son, I know!'; Joseph's blessing, 'a fruitful vine by a spring'.

Jacob buried at Machpelah; the brothers' fear, 'What if Joseph bears a grudge?'; 'We are your slaves!'; 'Do not be afraid. Am I in the place of God?'; 50:20; 'I will provide for you and your little ones'.
life.note: The owner's wording 'You intended to harm me, but God intended it for good' is the NIV (copyrighted); the page quotes the BSB: 'As for you, what you intended against me for evil, God intended for good...'.

life.text: Died at 110; saw Ephraim's sons to the third generation; Machir's sons brought up on his knees; the oath about his bones; embalmed and placed in a coffin in Egypt (the last verse of Genesis). Exodus 1:8, a king who did not know Joseph; Exodus 13:19, Moses took the bones; Joshua 24:32, buried at Shechem in Jacob's plot, an inheritance for Joseph's descendants; Hebrews 11:22.
Moses was the great-grandson of Levi (Levi, Kohath, Amram, Moses).
life.note: Fact 'When' and the Moses card in the circle.

life.text: Matthew 1:16, Jacob the father of Joseph the husband of Mary; Matthew 2:13-14, the dream and the flight to Egypt. John 4:5, 'the plot of ground that Jacob had given to his son Joseph'. Matthew 26:15, thirty pieces of silver.

names_and_art.text: Egyptian name Zaphenath-paneah (Genesis 41:45). Orthodox: 'Righteous Joseph the Patriarch' and 'Joseph the Fair' (OCA); 'Joseph the All-Comely' on Holy Monday (St Nicholas Russian Orthodox Church, McKinney, Texas, Priest Seraphim Holland, 2010). Yusuf in Arabic and the Quran; the Quran gives him a whole chapter, sura 12 (Jewish Encyclopedia, 'Joseph').
names_and_art.note: GOARCH and other pages for the Holy Monday synaxarion render by script and fetched empty; the parish page is the evidence for 'All-Comely'.

names_and_art.text: OCA: 'Before his death around 1700 B. C.'; 'As the father of Manassah and Ephraim, Saint Joseph is placed at the head of two of the tribes of Israel.'
names_and_art.note: Page: 'The OCA dates Joseph's death to about 1700 BC.'

names_and_art.text: The robe: the Hebrew word pas is found five times, all for Joseph's robe (Genesis 37:3, 23, 32) and Tamar's (2 Samuel 13:18-19). Strong's: 'properly, the palm (of the hand) or sole (of the foot) ... by implication (plural) a long and sleeved tunic (perhaps simply a wide one ...) -- (divers) colours'. The KJV: 'a coat of many colours'.
names_and_art.note: Myth 1. The NASB's 'varicolored' and 'long-sleeved' (copyrighted) were read but are not quoted.

names_and_art.text: The pictures chosen for their faces: Rembrandt's Joseph, turbaned and gentle, guiding his father's hand; Ivanov's young Joseph pointing to heaven in the prison.

said.text: Acts 7:9-10 (Stephen); Psalm 105:17-19; Sirach 49:15 (WEB; in Catholic and Orthodox Bibles); 1 Clement 4 ('Envy made Joseph be persecuted unto death, and to come into bondage'); Basil, Letter 2 ('He who is enamoured of chastity dwells upon the history of Joseph...'); Ambrose, On the Duties of the Clergy 1.24 ('How meek he was in slavery...'); Chrysostom, Homilies on John 71 ('Who then before Moses was patient? The blessed and noble Joseph...').
said.source: BSB; shared/web-world-english-bible.txt; shared/anf01.txt; shared/npnf208.txt; shared/npnf210.txt (book 1 begins at line 1367, chapter 24 at 3062); shared/npnf114.txt (Homily 71 at line 25627).
said.note: Basil's letter 2 is to Gregory of Nazianzus, about the monastic life; the passage is on reading the lives of holy men as models.

later.text: Tertullian, Ad Nationes 2.8 (about 197): 'For that Serapis of yours was originally one of our own saints called Joseph'; the turban's 'peck-like shape ... marks the memory of his corn-provisioning'.
later.source: shared/anf03.txt, chapter heading 'Serapis a Perversion of Joseph'.
later.note: Tertullian's retelling has slips (Joseph 'the youngest', a slave 'in the family of Pharaoh', Pharaoh's daughter as his wife); the ANF editor notes his memory errors. The page quotes only the Serapis line and says it is his claim.

later.text: Ambrose, On the Duties of the Clergy 2.16: 'For if he had given it to a few there would have been none for most.' Ambrose, On the Holy Spirit 3.17: 'Joseph was sold, Jesus Christ was bought, the one to slavery, the Other to death'; 'In one place the sale is for twenty pieces, in the other for thirty.'
later.source: shared/npnf210.txt (Duties book 2 begins at line 5545, chapter 16 at 6736; On the Holy Spirit book 3 at 14670, chapter 17 at 16380).

later.text: Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts 17, on Acts 7:9: 'Though they had no fault to find with him, and though he came on purpose to bring them their food, they thus ill-treated him.' Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew 84: 'What then did Joseph? He held his peace, and thus is condemned, even as Christ is also. For all those things are types of these.'
later.source: shared/npnf111.txt line 9733; shared/npnf110.txt line 46571 (Homily 84 begins at 46234).
later.note: The NPNF footnote says some editions omit Chrysostom's sentence 'Here again, the type of Christ' in Homily 17 and replace it with 'Joseph is a type of Him'. The page does not quote that sentence; it quotes the next one, which is in both.

later.text: Holy Monday: 'Monday of Holy Week commemorates the blessed and Noble Joseph the All-Comely and the fig tree which was cursed and withered by the Lord.' The parish page lists the parallels: sold for silver, cast into a pit and prison, silent, feeding his people with bread.
later.note: Paraphrased on the page (a modern text, not public domain); only its title is quoted, in the citation.

later.text: Jewish Encyclopedia, Joseph (1906): the name Zelikah in the Sefer ha-Yashar 'following Arabic sources'; Yusuf and Zulaikha 'a favorite love-song in the East'; Arabic tradition credits him with Memphis, the obelisks and the pyramids; 'According to most rabbinical authorities, Joseph's coffin was sunk in the Nile'; Serah daughter of Asher showed Moses; Moses threw a pebble and called; the coffin floated up.
later.note: The JE also says he drank no wine in his twenty-two years away (Shabbat 139a); cut from the page for space.

later.text: Gregory of Tours, History of the Franks 1.10: in Babylonia of Egypt 'Joseph built wonderful granaries of squared stone and rubble'; 'wide at the base and narrow at the top'; 'these granaries are to be seen at the present day'. Brehaut's note: 'The pyramids, apparently'.
later.note: Myth 3. That the pyramids are royal tombs is common knowledge and carries no cite.

feasts.text: OCA: 'Righteous Joseph the Patriarch', 'Commemorated on March 31'; 'also commemorated on the Sunday of the Holy Fathers, and on Great and Holy Monday.'
feasts.note: The Hermitage icon by Osip Chirikov (the page's gallery) is inscribed 'Месяцъ мартъ 31 число', the 31st of March, read by eye.

feasts.text: Lutheran Church–Missouri Synod: 31 March, 'Joseph, Patriarch', remembered 'for his moral uprightness (Genesis 39) and for his willingness to forgive his brothers'.

Roman Martyrology: no entry for Joseph the patriarch in the 1916 English edition (index and text searched: only Joseph the Just, Joseph of Arimathea, St Joseph the spouse and later Josephs) nor in the 2004 edition as GCatholic prints it in English (all twelve months searched for 'Jacob', 'son of Jacob' and 'patriarch Joseph'; Abraham on 9 October and Moses on 4 September are there, which shows the listing holds the Old Testament saints). 24 December commemorates all the holy ancestors of Christ; Joseph is not one of them by descent, so the page does not claim him there.
feasts.note: The 1969 Calendarium Romanum's litany names no Joseph but the spouse of Mary.

feasts.text: Church of England (Common Worship) and the Episcopal Church (Lesser Feasts and Fasts 2022): only Joseph of Nazareth (19 March) and Joseph of Arimathea; no day for the patriarch. The ELCA list has none.

pictures.text: Band, the owner's choice (the Rembrandt band, joseph-band.jpg, is retired; the card cut from it, joseph-card.jpg, stays): Joseph Recognised by His Brothers (Joseph reconnu par ses frères), Anne-Louis Girodet, 1789, École nationale supérieure des Beaux-Arts, Paris. Commons licence 'Public domain' read on the file page (photograph by VladoubidoOo). The file is only 987 x 768 and no larger copy is on Commons: saved at its own size (not enlarged), q88. posM 75% 30%, posD 72% 25% (Joseph's face at about 72% across, 27% down).

Portrait, the owner's choice (the Ivanov painting, joseph-2.jpg, is retired): Joseph Faithful in Prison, a Bible picture card published by the Providence Lithograph Company, 1907 (Genesis 39:20 to 40:15). Commons licence 'Public domain'. 770 x 876, saved at its own size, q88.

Gallery 1: Joseph, from Jacob and His Twelve Sons, Francisco de Zurbarán, between 1640 and 1645, Auckland Castle, Bishop Auckland. Commons licence tag {{PD-Art|PD-old-auto-1923|deathyear=1664}}. 1023 x 2000 on Commons (source: a newspaper photograph); cropped to the upper 56% at 942 x 1120, 137 KB.
pictures.note: The series of thirteen (Jacob and his twelve sons) at Auckland Castle: Wikipedia's Joseph (Genesis) infobox names the series; thirteen life-size portraits, twelve at Auckland Castle (Benjamin at Grimsthorpe), per Wikipedia's Jacob and His Twelve Sons, used as a lead; that article dates the series 1641 to 1658, Commons 1640 to 1645: the page says the 1640s.

pictures.text: Gallery 2: Righteous Joseph the Fair (Праведный Иосиф Прекрасный), an icon by Osip Semenovich Chirikov, 1800s, 31 x 25.3 cm, the State Hermitage Museum (ЭРЖ-2518, from the church of the Marble Palace). Commons licence tag {{PD-old}}. 787 x 960 on Commons; the outer frame trimmed to 692 x 913, 230 KB.
pictures.note: Small scan: the face is clear but small at column width. A taste call for the owner.

could_not_verify: The Holy Monday synaxarion and kontakion in a public-domain English translation: GOARCH and OMHKSEA pages fetched empty (script-rendered). The page paraphrases the parish page instead and quotes no hymn.
An Armenian commemoration on 26 July (Wikipedia, uncited): not checked, not printed.
A Coptic day for Joseph the patriarch: not found in the shared Coptic calendar list; not printed.
Joseph's Tomb near Nablus: left out (disputed, and nothing checked from a primary source).
The Roman Martyrology of 2004 was checked through GCatholic's English listing only, not the Latin book.

checker_2026_09_25.checked: One light pass on 2026-09-25. Read the page and this file whole. Checked against the fetched texts: the four number tiles (Genesis 37:2, 28; 41:46; 45:6; 50:22-26), the OCA life (Joseph the Fair, about 1700 BC, head of two tribes, also on the Sunday of the Holy Fathers and Great and Holy Monday), the LSB calendar (31 March, uprightness and forgiving his brothers), Tertullian Ad Nationes 2.8 on Serapis, Ambrose on selling the grain (Duties book 2), Chrysostom on Acts 7 (Homily 17) and on his silence (Matthew, Homily 84), Ambrose on the twenty and thirty pieces, Strong's 6446, the Jewish Encyclopedia on Zelikah, the pyramids, the coffin in the Nile, Serah and the pebble. Anglican calendars: not present. Commons licences: all four public domain. Card looked at: Joseph's face centred, eyes about 38 percent; Jacob's head leans in at the left, as the painting has it. verify-quotes exit 0; saints-test passed; measure-sheet leftGap 90, rightGap 212, sheetTallerThanFacts 0.
changed: Did you know? (Tertullian): it printed the same line the 'Is he a saint?' section quotes. Rewritten to tell of the grain-measure headdress instead, with its own quotation ('marks the memory of his corn-provisioning'), added to joseph.quotes.json.
